question: Which kernels actually own the W7900 AR prompt-processing (prefill) wall at the exact rows the published C1-C8 matrix produces, and is the deficit caused by an undeclared dispatch route as the task-#12 premise assumed?
answer: No. The shipping route never runs a pack8 kernel. Dense prefill is owned by the Q4_T16 WMMA family, and the device is already 94% busy, so the deficit is per-kernel efficiency at rows 35-67, not a dispatch declaration.
model: /models/gguf/Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf (17106773984 bytes) as loaded by hipengine.LLM with the default policy, i.e. the same route the published C1-C8 matrix uses. The q4_k_pack8 policy (QWEN35_DENSE_H5120_GEOMETRY) is a different model/route and appears nowhere in this trace.
quant: MOSTLY_Q4_K_M on the wire; tiled Q4_T16 / Q5_T16 / Q6_K_T16 micro-tile tiers at execution time depending on tensor
hardware: epyc / AMD Radeon Pro W7900 gfx1100 / Ryzen 9 5950X
workload_shape: one prompt (suite id code_merge_intervals, 161 chars, 35 prompt rows), max_tokens=1, three sequential generate() calls, production execution profile
protocol: All kernels prebuilt outside the profiler, compiler-version file precomputed, HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1 so the profiled process never spawns hipcc/clang, per docs/KERNELS.md. Iterations split at argmax_rows_stage2 (one per generate call). The steady-state third iteration is reported. busy = sum of kernel durations, span = last_end - first_start.

implications.task_12_premise_falsified: Every pack8-vs-T16 number in the campaign, including this session's dual-WMMA rejection, describes a route the published C1-C8 rows do not execute. Declaring GGUF_Q4_PACK8_DUAL_WMMA_SILU_PREFILL, or GGUF_Q4_PACK8_WMMA_BULK_PREFILL, or any _POLICIES entry, could not have moved a published row, because the pack8 leaf is never reached by the default-policy model the matrix loads.
implications.no_control_headroom: At 94% device utilization inside a 256 ms span, there is no launch-gap, host-work, or admission slack to recover at these shapes. The wall is kernel time.
implications.real_headroom_is_arithmetic: The three T16 WMMA prefill kernels account for 89% of busy time. For the FFN pair geometry (rows=35, 5120x17408), one pass over the Q4 weights is ~22 ms and the equivalent compute bound is ~27 ms, against 140 ms measured in the q4_t16 shared_b bucket, i.e. roughly 5x off both rooflines. Closing that is kernel work on the T16 family, which is the only way C1-C3 improves.
implications.fused_coverage_is_small: The fused unequal-dual T16 owner covers 24 launches per iteration while silu_mul_separate_out runs 64 times per iteration, so most FFN gate/up pairs still execute as two projections plus a separate SiLU. Because SiLU itself is 0.3 ms total, fusing the rest is worth far less than the shared_b kernel's 140 ms, and should not be mistaken for the main lever.
implications.scale_of_the_remaining_gap: The published C1-C8 deficit is 11.0% at C1 (148.72 vs 1472.49 tok/s), not the 2.26x in the campaign notes; 2.26x is a pp512 whole-prompt throughput comparison in a different regime. An 11% gap on a 94%-utilized device needs about 27 ms per request, which is within the noise of a single kernel's tile-shape choice at rows 35-67.

correctness_gate: Observation only. No engine file, session flag, or arithmetic was modified; the driver used the public LLM API, and the profiler wrappers were external to the process.
consequence_for_objective: The remaining C1-C3 path is a T16 small-row kernel-efficiency question with a named 140 ms target, and the AR C2/C3 deficit (#11) is the same wall, not a separate one. Task #12's dispatch-declaration framing is closed as a false premise.
